page.layout: One page of text. At the top, a full-width centred epigraph (Apoc. 15), then a decorative rule. Below it, a centred heading "COROLLARIA" with the subheading "Respondentis.", then a numbered list of theses 1–7 in the left-hand column, and "IMPER." set at the right below them.

main_text.p: Nostrum est succinere Sanctis stantibus super mare vitreum, habentibus citharas Dei & cantantibus canticum Mosis servi Dei, & canticum agni, dicendo; Magna & mirabilia sunt opera tua Domine Deus Omnipotens, justæ & veræ sunt viæ tuæ Domine Rex Sanctorum. Quis non timeat te Domine, & magnificet nomen tuum! Apoc. 15. vers. 2. 3.
main_text.head: COROLLARIA
Respondentis.
main_text.p: 1. Nomen Jehova Deo Opt. Max. ita est proprium ut nulli communicetur creaturæ.
3. Nomen Elohim non perinde Deo & creaturis, quibus tribuitur, convenit
4. Non datur quadruplex S. Scripturæ sensus
5. Cabala Rabinorum Theoretica, quam vocant, & Practica vanitas est.
7. Miraculorum 76. à Judæis Mosi assignatorum numerus non est accuratus.

page.notes: No running head, page number, catchword or signature is printed. The decorative rule between the epigraph and the heading is an ornament, not text. The first letter of thesis 1 is a large initial N, joined to the word "omen". "Jehova" is set in small capitals in the print; the rendering here is approximate. The Hebrew line under thesis 4 is a continuation of that thesis, printed on its own line; the reading is uncertain and is marked [?]. The epigraph's italic passages are marked with <i>, and the long s is written as a plain s throughout.
